The SI module for the MY component

Source: R/adult-MY-SI.R
SI.Rd

This implements an SI compartmental model for mosquito infection dynamics. Adult mosquitoes are either susceptible or infected and infectious, and infected mosquitoes die rather than recover from infection. In its simplest form, the dynamics describe adult mosquito ecology \((M)\) and infection dynamics \((Y)\): $$ \begin{array}{rl} dM/dt &= \Lambda - g M \\ dY/dt &= fq\kappa(M-Y) - g Y \end{array} $$ It is equivalent to an S-I compartmental model under a change of variables \(S = M-Y\) and \(I=Y.\)

The SI module is a generalized implementation of the S-I model:

  • the module adds a variable to compute the density of parous mosquitoes

  • mosquito ecology and infection dynamics are spatial – a patch-based meta-population model – so state variables and most parameters are vectors of length nPatches. The dispersal matrix has dimension nPatches \(\times\) nPatches

  • biting by infectious mosquitoes is computed at time \(t\) as if the infected mosquitoes had survived through the EIP \((\tau)\).

  • parameters describe egg laying by the adult mosquito population

  • several of the core bionomic parameters are set up as ports and designed to be computed as a changing baseline that can be modified by vector control

The SI Vignette discusses the model family, and the module design and implementation.

Note

Parity is computed during parsing as \(P/M\) and its orbit is stored as parity.

The orbits of fqZ and EIR are computed and stored by xds_solve by the functions that parse the outputs.

State Variables

M

density of adult mosquitoes

P

density of parous adult mosquitoes

Y

density of infected adult mosquitoes

Dynamical Terms

Lambda or \(\Lambda\)

the number of adult mosquitoes emerging, per patch, per day, computed by Emergence

kappa or \(\kappa\)

net infectiousness: the probability a mosquito becomes infected after blood feeding on a human, is computed by Transmission

Parameters

f

blood feeding rates — use setup_f or setup_blood_feeding_rates

q

human fraction — use setup_q or setup_human_fractions

g

mosquito mortality rate — use setup_g or setup_mosquito_mortality

eip or \(\tau\)

extrinsic incubation period — use setup_eip

sigma or \(\sigma\)

emigration rate — use setup_sigma or setup_mosy_emigration

mu or \(\mu\)

emigration loss fraction — use setup_mu or setup_emigration_loss

K

mosquito dispersal matrix — use setup_K_matrix

nu or \(\nu\)

the oviposition rate: the number of egg batches laid in each patch, per mosquito, per day — use setup_nu or setup_egg_batch_rates

eggsPerBatch or \(\Gamma\)

the number of eggs per batch

After basic setup, change_MY_pars can be used for static parameters, or for parameters that are set up as static ports (the default). Use advanced setup to modify dynamic ports.

Survival and Dispersal

Mosquito survival and dispersal are described by a single matrix, \(\Omega.\)

The parameter \(g\) is interpreted as the per-capita mortality rate for mosquitoes while they are in a patch. Mosquitoes emigrate from patches at the per-capita rates \(\sigma\), and some fraction of emigrating mosquitoes is lost (\(\mu\)). The combined rate of mortality and loss during emigration is $$g + \mu \sigma.$$

The columns of the mosquito dispersal matrix \((K)\) sum to zero. The default matrix is all zeros, but for non-trivial dispersal matrices: $$\mbox{diag}\left(K\right)=-1$$ and the non-diagonal elements are fractions of surviving mosquitoes that arrive at another patch after a flight bout. (If there is any population loss associated with emigration, it goes in the term \(\mu\).)

The matrix \(\Omega\) is computed as $$\Omega = \mbox{diag}\left(g + \sigma \mu \right) - K \cdot \mbox{diag}\left(\sigma \left(1-\mu\right)\right)$$

Blood Feeding

The overall blood feeding rate (\(f\)) and the human fraction (\(q\)) are configured as ports. By default, the baseline values are constant, but they can be modified by control. At their baseline, the parameter values ought to be subject to some natural constraints:

  • If no blood hosts are available, then it should be true that \(f=0.\)

  • If no humans are available, then it should be true that \(q=0.\)

  • If only humans are available, then it should be true that \(q=1.\)

Using advanced setup options, the blood feeding parameters can be forced by variables describing resource availability or weather.

ODE

Ecology

Adult mosquitoes emerge from aquatic habitats at rate \(\Lambda\) and disperse and die according to \(\Omega\): $$ dM/dt = \Lambda - \Omega \cdot M $$ The model also computes the density of parous adult mosquitoes: those that have blood fed at least once: $$ dP/dt = fq(M-P) - \Omega \cdot P \\ $$

Infection Dynamics

Given the per-capita daily rate of human blood feeding \((fq)\) and net infectiousness \((\kappa)\), the FoI for mosquitoes is \(fq\kappa\). Changes in the density of infected mosquitoes are given by: $$ dY/dt = fq\kappa(M-Y) - \Omega \cdot Y \\ $$

DTS

Ecology

Adult mosquitoes emerge from aquatic habitats at rate \(\Lambda\) and disperse and die according to \(\Omega\). The one-day update in Update_MYt.SI is: $$M_t = \Lambda + e^{-\Omega}\cdot M_{t-1}$$ The model also computes the density of parous adult mosquitoes: those that have blood fed at least once: $$P_t = e^{-\Omega}\cdot\left[(1-e^{-fq})(M_{t-1}-P_{t-1}) + P_{t-1}\right]$$

Infection Dynamics

Given the per-capita daily rate of human blood feeding \((fq)\) and net infectiousness \((\kappa)\), the FoI for mosquitoes is \(fq\kappa\). The density of infected mosquitoes is updated by: $$Y_t = e^{-\Omega}\cdot\left[(1-e^{-fq\kappa})(M_{t-1}-Y_{t-1}) + Y_{t-1}\right]$$

Infective Biting

Infective biting density is defined as the number of human infectious bites by the mosquito population in each patch, each day. In SI, infective biting density is computed if infected mosquitoes at time \(t\), \(Y(t),\) had survived and dispersed through an EIP of \(\tau\) days \(e^{- \Omega \tau}\).

\(Z\)

density of infectious mosquitoes, imputed from \(Y\)

fqZ

Infective biting density: the number of infectious bites, per patch, per day $$fqZ = e^{-\Omega \tau} \cdot \left( f q Y \right) $$

fqM

Human biting density: the number of bites on humans, per patch, per day

Note that \(e^{-\Omega \tau}\) is computed with the matrix exponential function expm

The EIR

\(fqZ\) is the dynamical term computed by F_fqZ.SI. It is called by compute_EIR (in Transmission) to compute and store EIR, the local daily EIR \((E)\). Note that fqZ is a vector of length nPatches but the local EIR is a vector of length nStrata. The XY interface uses information about humans and mosquitoes to build the biting distribution matrix, \(\beta,\) and if there are no visitors, then $$E = \beta \cdot fqZ$$

The HBR

Since estimates of the EIR are computed by taking the product of the human biting rate (HBR or \(B\)) and the sporozoite rate, there is interest in knowing \(fqM\) and \(B.\) The quantity fqM is computed by F_fqM.SI. The orbits of fqM and HBR are also computed during parsing, as $$B = \beta \cdot fqM$$

Egg Laying

G

the number of eggs laid, per patch, per day $$G = \nu M \Gamma $$

\(G\) is the dynamical term passed to EggLaying to distribute eggs among the habitats that are found in each patch.
